views.name: product_monthly_sales
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  mth,
  qty
FROM
  monthly_sales

params.description: Monthly quantity sold per product (one row per product per month).
params.when_to_use: Get total quantity sold for a specific product in a given month or range of months. | Trend analysis of product monthly quantity (time series by product). | Joining product monthly sales to product/dimension tables for enrichment (ensuring join keys preserve cardinality). | Composing higher-level aggregates (e.g., product quarter or product-year totals) by re-aggregating the monthly qty.
params.output_schema: product_id: identifier of the product — derives directly from monthly_sales.product_id | mth: month period (the grain dimension) — derives directly from monthly_sales.mth | qty: total quantity for that product in that month — derives directly from monthly_sales.qty
params.metric: qty = monthly_sales.qty  -- this view exposes the pre-aggregated monthly quantity per product. The value is expected to be an aggregate already computed in monthly_sales (i.e., total quantity for product_id and mth).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to product_monthly_sales_with_product on product_id — safe because product_monthly_sales is one row per (product_id, mth) and product_monthly_sales_with_product is a JOIN enrichment expected to be one-row-per-product (or one-row-per-product per mth if it includes mth); verify the sibling view's grain before joining to avoid duplication. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to latest_ticker_per_symbol on product_id (if product_id maps 1:1 to symbol) — safe when the ticker view returns a single row per symbol/product, so qty is not duplicated. | DO NOT join directly to orders_with_lines_and_customers without re-aggregating the orders/lines side to (product_id, mth) first — orders_with_lines_and_customers is a JOIN that can be one-to-many relative to product_monthly_sales and would multiply qty if joined at (product_id) or (product_id,mth) without aggregation. | DO NOT join directly to purchases_enriched or inventory_stock_by_location (if those are one-to-many by product and/or location) without first aggregating them to the same grain (product_id, mth) — otherwise the monthly qty measure will be duplicated. | When composing higher-level metrics (e.g., quarterly or yearly product qty), re-aggregate qty by summing over mth after grouping by the desired higher-level period and product_id: total_qty = SUM(qty) GROUP BY product_id, quarter/year. | When joining to dimension-like siblings (product info), prefer joins on product_id and ensure the dimension is one-row-per-product; if the dimension is one-to-many (e.g., product translations or multiple rows per product), collapse it (e.g., pick latest or aggregate) first. | If you need to join to web_daily_device_totals or web_demographics_unpivot, first transform those to the product-month grain (product_id, mth) — e.g., attribute web events to products and aggregate per mth — before joining, to avoid inflating qty. | General rule: this view's measures are safe to join to any table/view that is guaranteeably 1:1 or many-to-1 into (product_id, mth). For any N:1 or N:N where the other side has multiple rows per (product_id, mth), you must aggregate that other side to (product_id, mth) prior to joining, or join and then re-aggregate the qty appropriately.

views.description: Monthly aggregated sales per product (one row per product_id + mth) exposing qty and running totals useful for trend analysis, comparisons to budget, and time series joins with product attributes. | Use for: time series of sales for a product; compare actual monthly sales to budget; aggregate sales by product group after joining products/product_groups; compute growth rates month-over-month

views.name: product_monthly_sales_with_product
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ms.product_id,
  ms.mth,
  ms.qty,
  p.id AS id,
  p.name AS name,
  p.group_id AS group_id,
  pg.id AS id,
  pg.name AS name
FROM
  monthly_sales ms
  LEFT JOIN products p ON ms.product_id = p.id
  LEFT JOIN product_groups pg ON p.group_id = pg.id

params.description: Monthly sales quantities for each product, enriched with product and product-group attributes (one row per product_id × mth).
params.when_to_use: Report monthly quantity sold per product with product and product-group names/ids | Filter, group, or trend monthly product sales by product attributes or product group | As a base for further aggregation (e.g., product-month → product-quarter or product-year) or for joining to dimensions that are 1:1 to product or product-group
params.output_schema: product_id: product identifier from monthly_sales.product_id (grain column) | mth: month of the sales measurement from monthly_sales.mth (grain column) | qty: reported quantity sold for that product in that month from monthly_sales.qty (measure/metric at the product_id × mth grain) | id: product id from products.id (enrichment of product attributes; note SQL aliases duplicate the name 'id' for product and product_group — see grounded_columns for exact sources) | name: product name from products.name (enrichment attribute) | group_id: product.group_id from products.group_id (pointer to the product group) | id: product_group id from product_groups.id (enrichment attribute for the product's group; aliased the same 'id' label in SQL) | name: product_group name from product_groups.name (enrichment attribute for the product's group; aliased the same 'name' label in SQL)
params.grounded_columns: monthly_sales.product_id | monthly_sales.mth | monthly_sales.qty | products.id | products.name | products.group_id | product_groups.id | product_groups.name
params.metric: qty = monthly_sales.qty  -- a base (non-aggregated) quantity measure at the product_id × mth grain | product_monthly_row (implicit) = one row per (monthly_sales.product_id, monthly_sales.mth) as produced by the FROM monthly_sales plus LEFT JOIN enrichment
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to product dimension tables or views keyed 1:1 on products.id (for example a canonical products dimension) on product_id = products.id — safe because this view already has at most one row per product_id×mth and products is 1:1 on id so qty won't be duplicated | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to product_groups (or a product_groups dimension) on group_id = product_groups.id — safe when product_groups is 1:1 on id because each product row references at most one group | do NOT join without care to one-to-many tables or views on product_id (for example: orders_with_lines_and_customers or any order-lines-level view) because those are many rows per product_id and would multiply the qty measure; if you must join to a one-to-many set, first aggregate that set to product_id (or product_id×mth) so the join stays cardinality-safe | do NOT join to web_daily_device_totals or other time-grained web tables without aligning granularity: monthly_sales is at mth granularity, so either (a) roll web data up to month and join on (product_id, mth) if web has product context, or (b) aggregate product_monthly_sales up to the larger granularity you need before joining | when composing higher-level metrics (e.g., total_qty_by_product or total_qty_by_group over a time window), aggregate qty (SUM(qty)) after joining any dimensions that are 1:1; if joining any N:1 or 1:N relation that would duplicate rows, re-aggregate the many-side first | joins safe without re-aggregation: any table/view that is strictly 1:1 to (product_id) or to (product_group.id) and does not introduce additional multiplicity (e.g., a single-row product attributes view keyed by products.id) | recommended pattern to avoid accidental duplication: FROM product_monthly_sales_with_product pmswp LEFT JOIN (<many-side aggregated to product_id or product_id,mth>) AS agg ON matching keys — then use SUM(agg.metric) or combine SUM(pmswp.qty) as needed

views.description: Monthly sales per product enriched with product and product group attributes. Useful when questions need product names, group names, or to filter/aggregate by group. | Use for: list top-selling products by month with product names; compare sales across product groups; filter monthly sales for specific product attributes

views.name: purchases_enriched
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.id,
  p.purchased,
  p.brewery_id,
  p.product_id,
  p.qty,
  p.cost,
  b.id AS id,
  b.name AS name,
  prod.id AS id,
  prod.name AS name,
  prod.group_id AS group_id
FROM
  purchases p
  LEFT JOIN breweries b ON p.brewery_id = b.id
  LEFT JOIN products prod ON p.product_id = prod.id

params.description: Row-level enriched purchases: one row per purchase with joined brewery and product attributes.
params.when_to_use: Fetch individual purchase records together with the brewery name and product attributes. | Filter or group purchases by product attributes (product.name, product.group_id) while preserving purchase-level detail. | Join purchase-level measures (qty, cost) to dimensions that are one-to-one with purchases (for example a purchases-level annotation table) or to aggregate further (e.g., monthly totals) while treating this view as the base grain of purchases.
params.output_schema: id: purchase id (from purchases.id) — primary key / row grain | purchased: purchase timestamp/date (from purchases.purchased) | brewery_id: foreign key referencing breweries (from purchases.brewery_id) | product_id: foreign key referencing products (from purchases.product_id) | qty: quantity purchased (from purchases.qty) | cost: cost of the purchase (from purchases.cost) | id: brewery id (from breweries.id) — note: aliased in the SQL; this is the brewery's id | name: brewery name (from breweries.name) — note: aliased in the SQL; this is the brewery's name | id: product id (from products.id) — note: aliased in the SQL; this is the product's id | name: product name (from products.name) — note: aliased in the SQL; this is the product's name | group_id: product group id (from products.group_id)
params.grounded_columns: purchases.id | purchases.purchased | purchases.brewery_id | purchases.product_id | purchases.qty | purchases.cost | breweries.id | breweries.name | products.id | products.name | products.group_id
params.metric: qty = purchases.qty (base measure at purchase row grain; not aggregated in this view) | cost = purchases.cost (base measure at purchase row grain; not aggregated in this view)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a dimension that is one-to-one with purchases (or keyed by purchases.id) — e.g., a purchases-level annotation table — on purchases.id (safe because this view is one row per purchases.id, so measures qty and cost are not duplicated). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to breweries (or a brewery-level view) on brewery_id = breweries.id is safe only if that target is one-row-per-brewery; joining to a brewery dimension will not duplicate purchase rows because multiple purchases can reference the same brewery but the join is many(purchase)->one(brewery), which preserves purchase row multiplicity (does not inflate each purchase's measures). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to products (or a product-level view) on product_id = products.id is safe only if that target is one-row-per-product; the join is many(purchase)->one(product) and will not duplicate purchase measures. | Do NOT join this view directly to any table or view that is one-to-many from purchase (i.e., that can return multiple rows per purchases.id) without re-aggregation. Examples to avoid: joining to an orders_with_lines_and_customers-like view keyed at order line level or any order-lines table where multiple rows match the same purchases.id. Such joins would multiply rows and duplicate qty/cost unless you first aggregate the many-side back to one row per purchases.id (e.g., SUM(...) GROUP BY purchases.id) or aggregate this view instead. | When composing aggregations: if you aggregate purchases_enriched (for example SUM(cost) GROUP BY product_id, products.group_id, month(purchased)), you can safely join that aggregated result to product_monthly_sales (an aggregate) or product_monthly_sales_with_product (join) only if keys and time grain align; otherwise reconcile grains by aggregating to a common grain before joining to avoid double-counting. | Avoid joining to sibling AGG views (product_monthly_sales, inventory_stock_by_location) directly expecting row-level preservation — those are pre-aggregated and must be aligned by keys and grain. If you need purchase-level measures combined with those aggregates, aggregate purchases_enriched to the same grain first.

views.description: Purchase transactions enriched with product and brewery attributes. One row per purchase transaction (id). Useful for cost analysis, supplier performance, and joining to inventory/purchases timelines. | Use for: total cost by brewery or product over a period; match purchases to inventory receipts; supplier analysis: average cost per product from each brewery

views.name: inventory_stock_by_location
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  location_id,
  SUM(qty) AS qty_on_hand
FROM
  inventory
GROUP BY
  product_id,
  location_id

params.description: Per-product per-location inventory totals: the quantity on hand (sum of qty) for each product_id and location_id.
params.when_to_use: Get current inventory levels aggregated at the product × location grain. | Join inventory totals onto product or location dimension details without changing totals. | Compute higher-level inventory aggregates (e.g., product-level or location-level) by re-aggregating this view. | Report stock availability per store/warehouse, or drive replenishment logic per product-location.
params.output_schema: product_id: identifier of the product — derived directly from inventory.product_id (GROUP BY key). | location_id: identifier of the inventory location (warehouse/store) — derived directly from inventory.location_id (GROUP BY key). | qty_on_hand: sum of inventory quantities at the product_id × location_id grain — derived from SUM(inventory.qty) as qty_on_hand in the SELECT.
params.metric: qty_on_hand = SUM(inventory.qty)  -- aggregate computed at GROUP BY (product_id, location_id)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a product dimension (e.g., products or product_monthly_sales_with_product) on product_id — safe because inventory_stock_by_location is one row per product_id × location_id; joining to a one-row-per-product dimension (keyed by product_id) will not duplicate qty_on_hand. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a location dimension (e.g., locations table) on location_id — safe because the location dimension is one-row-per-location; qty_on_hand remains correctly attributed per product-location row. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many fact/detail tables (for example: orders_with_lines_and_customers, purchases_enriched, web_daily_device_totals if keyed at a finer grain than product_id×location_id) without re-aggregation or deduplication first — such joins would multiply inventory_stock_by_location rows and thus duplicate qty_on_hand unless you re-aggregate the combined result back to product_id×location_id. | If you need inventory totals combined with another fact that is at a lower grain (e.g., order lines per order_id × product_id or purchase lines per purchase_id × product_id), either: (a) aggregate that other fact to product_id (or product_id×location_id if it has location) before joining, or (b) join and then re-aggregate SUM(qty_on_hand) grouped by the intended grain. This prevents measure inflation from one-to-many joins. | When computing product-level totals from this view, aggregate qty_on_hand by product_id (SUM(qty_on_hand) GROUP BY product_id) rather than joining to a product-level table expecting one row per product; doing so preserves correctness. | Avoid joining to sibling AGG views at incompatible grains without alignment: for example, joining this view to product_monthly_sales (which is per product_id×month) must align on product_id and either filter/aggregate month or expand inventory by month externally; otherwise you may unintentionally replicate inventory rows across months. | Safe composition example patterns: (1) SELECT p.*, s.qty_on_hand FROM product_dim p LEFT JOIN inventory_stock_by_location s ON p.product_id = s.product_id AND s.location_id = 'WH-1' — safe if product_dim is one-row-per-product and location_id is constrained. (2) To get product totals: SELECT product_id, SUM(qty_on_hand) AS product_qty FROM inventory_stock_by_location GROUP BY product_id. | Unsafe composition example patterns: (1) SELECT * FROM inventory_stock_by_location i JOIN orders_with_lines_and_customers o ON i.product_id = o.product_id — unsafe if orders_with_lines_and_customers has many rows per product because i.qty_on_hand will be duplicated across those order rows unless you aggregate or limit the join. | Planner note: this view's measures are safe to be treated as additive at the product_id and location_id keys. Any join that preserves a 1:1 or many:1 relationship from inventory_stock_by_location to the other side will not duplicate measures; joins that create 1:many from inventory_stock_by_location to the other side will duplicate measures and require re-aggregation.

views.description: Current inventory stock quantities aggregated by product and location. One row per product_id + location_id exposing total qty on hand. Useful for replenishment, location-level stock checks, and joining to locations or products. | Use for: how much stock of a product exists at a location; identify products below minimums when joined to product_minimums; prepare pick lists by available qty at locations

views.name: orders_with_lines_and_customers
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ol.id AS id,
  ol.order_id,
  ol.product_id,
  ol.qty,
  ol.amount,
  o.id AS id,
  o.customer_id,
  o.ordered,
  o.delivery,
  c.id AS id,
  c.name AS name
FROM
  orderlines ol
  LEFT JOIN orders o ON ol.order_id = o.id
  LEFT JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id

params.description: Row-level join of orderlines to their parent orders and the orders' customers; answers questions about individual order line items enriched with order and customer attributes.
params.when_to_use: Fetch detailed order-line records along with order-level timestamps and customer name for reporting or downstream aggregation. | Compose aggregations by grouping on orderline-level fields (product_id, order_id, customer_id) to compute sales, quantities, or counts. | Filter orderlines by order attributes (ordered, delivery) or customer attributes (name) before aggregation.
params.output_schema: id: orderline id (from orderlines.id aliased as id) — unique identifier at the view grain | order_id: foreign key to orders (from orderlines.order_id) | product_id: product identifier for the order line (from orderlines.product_id) | qty: quantity ordered on the order line (from orderlines.qty) | amount: monetary amount for the order line (from orderlines.amount) | id: order id (from orders.id) — note: the source SQL aliases multiple tables' id columns as the same name; when used programmatically callers must disambiguate which 'id' they need (this view's grain is the orderline id) | customer_id: foreign key to customers for the order (from orders.customer_id) | ordered: order timestamp or date (from orders.ordered) | delivery: delivery timestamp or date (from orders.delivery) | id: customer id (from customers.id) — aliased same as other id columns in SQL; actual underlying source is customers.id | name: customer name (from customers.name)
params.grounded_columns: orderlines.id | orderlines.order_id | orderlines.product_id | orderlines.qty | orderlines.amount | orders.id | orders.customer_id | orders.ordered | orders.delivery | customers.id | customers.name
params.metric: qty = orderlines.qty  -- base numeric measure representing units on the line | amount = orderlines.amount  -- base monetary measure for the line | line_count = COUNT(orderlines.id)  -- derived when aggregating: count of order lines | total_qty = SUM(orderlines.qty)  -- derived aggregation over the view's grain | total_amount = SUM(orderlines.amount)  -- derived aggregation over the view's grain
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to customers or orders on their primary key only when treating those tables as 1:1 for the keys present on this view — e.g., join to a customer-level dimension on customers.id = customer_id is safe because this view contains at most one row per orderline and customers.id is 1:1 to the customer row; joining to customers will not multiply orderline-level measures as long as customers is a strict dimension keyed by customers.id. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders on orders.id = order_id is safe for filtering or enriching because orders is 1:1 on orders.id; this view already LEFT JOINed orders but a planner composing additional attributes from an orders-level view (that is 1:1 on orders.id) will not duplicate the orderline measures. | do NOT join directly to any table or view that is one-to-many from these keys without re-aggregation first — for example, do NOT join to orderlines again, or to any shipments or tracking events table that has multiple rows per orderline or order, without aggregating those many-rows into 1 row per orderline (or order) first. Such joins would multiply measures like amount and qty. | do NOT join to sibling AGG views that are aggregated at a finer grain than this view's consumers expect unless aligning grain and using proper aggregation: e.g., joining to product_monthly_sales (aggregated by product+month) to get monthly metrics is only safe after grouping this view by product and month — otherwise you will either lose detail or double-count when duplicating rows. | When composing further aggregations: treat this view as having grain = orderlines.id. To get order-level totals, first aggregate the view by order_id (SUM(amount), SUM(qty), COUNT(DISTINCT id) if needed). To combine with product_monthly_sales (which is pre-aggregated), join on product_id and month after aggregating this view to the same (product, month) grain to avoid duplication. | Examples of safe compositions: | - Enrich aggregated orderline totals by customer attributes: aggregate this view by customer_id (SUM(amount), SUM(qty)) then join to a customer-dimension on customers.id = customer_id — safe because customer-dimension is 1:1. | - Compute per-order totals: aggregate by order_id (SUM(amount), SUM(qty)) using this view; do not then join back to orderlines without re-aggregating. | Examples of unsafe compositions: | - Joining this view directly to a shipments table with multiple shipments per orderline without pre-aggregating shipments will multiply orderline.amount and orderline.qty. | - Joining to a web_events table (many events per customer) on customers.id without first summarizing events to customer-level metrics will duplicate orderline measures.

views.description: Orders denormalized with their orderlines and customer attributes. One row per orderline (id from orderlines) to support revenue, order-level and customer-level analytics. | Use for: compute revenue per order or customer; list orderlines with customer names for fulfilment; analyze order lead times between ordered and delivery

views.name: web_daily_device_totals
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  day,
  pc,
  tablet,
  phone,
  (IFNULL(pc,0) + IFNULL(tablet,0) + IFNULL(phone,0)) AS total
FROM
  web_devices

params.description: Daily counts of web sessions or device-based events broken out by device category (pc, tablet, phone) with a computed daily total.
params.when_to_use: Report daily device distribution (pc/tablet/phone) for a specific date or date range | Compose time-series aggregations (e.g., rollup to weekly/monthly) from daily device totals | Join to date or calendar dimension to add labels or fiscal attributes (without changing measure cardinality) | Calculate device share percentages per day (pc/total, tablet/total, phone/total) | Use as a pre-aggregated input when computing downstream ratios or rates that require daily device-level totals
params.output_schema: day: calendar date representing the day of the measurement; comes directly from web_devices.day | pc: numeric count/metric for 'pc' device category on that day; comes directly from web_devices.pc | tablet: numeric count/metric for 'tablet' device category on that day; comes directly from web_devices.tablet | phone: numeric count/metric for 'phone' device category on that day; comes directly from web_devices.phone | total: numeric computed as IFNULL(pc,0) + IFNULL(tablet,0) + IFNULL(phone,0); derived in the view SQL
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a date/calendar dimension (e.g., calendar.day = web_daily_device_totals.day) — safe because web_daily_device_totals is one-row-per-day and the calendar dimension is one-row-per-day, so measures are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to singleton or one-to-one lookup tables keyed by day (if such exist) — safe because keys are one-to-one. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many event/detail tables (for example raw web_events or orders_with_lines_and_customers if it contains multiple rows per day) without re-aggregation on the many-side first, because joining a one-row-per-day pre-aggregate to a many-rows-per-day table will multiply this view's measures and overcount totals. | do NOT join to sibling aggregated views that are at a finer grain (e.g., per-session or per-user-per-day) without aggregating the finer-grained view up to day first — instead, aggregate the finer-grained data to day and then join on day, or join on day and use windowed-safe expressions that avoid double-counting. | When composing into larger aggregations (e.g., monthly totals), aggregate the numeric columns (pc, tablet, phone, total) using SUM(...) grouped by the target grain. Do not SUM an already-monthly-aggregated sibling view unless you are certain there is no overlapping aggregation. | Joining to other one-row-per-day pre-aggregates (e.g., another daily summary view) on day is safe — both sides represent the same grain so measures will not be duplicated. | If you need device-level joins (e.g., to a device-dimension keyed by device type), join on a device-type value after unpivoting this view (use web_demographics_unpivot or similar) — do not join to a device dimension by expanding this view into multiple rows without explicitly reshaping/aggregating, otherwise you may change cardinality unexpectedly.

views.description: Daily web device counts with a total visits measure. One row per day; normalizes device columns and provides a derived total measure for easy trend/ratio calculations. | Use for: device mix over time; percentage of traffic from mobile vs desktop; join with web_demographics by day

views.name: web_demographics_unpivot
views.body_sql:
SELECT day, 'M' AS letter, 'tw' AS channel_shortcut, m_tw_cnt AS cnt, m_tw_qty AS qty FROM web_demographics
UNION ALL
SELECT day, 'M' AS letter, 'fb' AS channel_shortcut, m_fb_cnt AS cnt, m_fb_qty AS qty FROM web_demographics
UNION ALL
SELECT day, 'F' AS letter, 'tw' AS channel_shortcut, f_tw_cnt AS cnt, f_tw_qty AS qty FROM web_demographics
UNION ALL
SELECT day, 'F' AS letter, 'fb' AS channel_shortcut, f_fb_cnt AS cnt, f_fb_qty AS qty FROM web_demographics

params.description: Provides per-day counts and quantities broken down by biological sex letter (M/F) and channel shortcut (tw/fb) by unpivoting columns from web_demographics into a tall shape.
params.when_to_use: Get daily counts or quantities by sex and channel (e.g., daily cnt for M on tw). | Filter/aggregate time series by letter and channel (e.g., sum qty for F across a date range and channel). | Use as a building block to join to date or small-dimension tables that do not duplicate rows, or to further aggregate (group) into larger grains (weekly/monthly) safely.
params.output_schema: day: day value copied directly from web_demographics.day (represents the date grain of the row). | letter: demographic letter 'M' or 'F' produced by the view (derived by literal in the SELECTs, representing sex). | channel_shortcut: channel code 'tw' or 'fb' produced by the view (derived by literal in the SELECTs, representing channel shorthand). | cnt: count metric derived from the corresponding web_demographics.*_cnt source columns (m_tw_cnt, m_fb_cnt, f_tw_cnt, f_fb_cnt). | qty: quantity metric derived from the corresponding web_demographics.*_qty source columns (m_tw_qty, m_fb_qty, f_tw_qty, f_fb_qty).
params.grounded_columns: web_demographics.day | web_demographics.m_tw_cnt | web_demographics.m_tw_qty | web_demographics.m_fb_cnt | web_demographics.m_fb_qty | web_demographics.f_tw_cnt | web_demographics.f_tw_qty | web_demographics.f_fb_cnt | web_demographics.f_fb_qty
params.metric: cnt = SELECTed directly from one of the base columns (m_tw_cnt | m_fb_cnt | f_tw_cnt | f_fb_cnt) depending on (letter, channel_shortcut). No aggregation performed in this view; values are row-level from web_demographics. | qty = SELECTed directly from one of the base columns (m_tw_qty | m_fb_qty | f_tw_qty | f_fb_qty) depending on (letter, channel_shortcut). No aggregation performed in this view.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a date or day-dimension table on day (e.g., date_dim.day = web_demographics_unpivot.day) — safe because this view is one row per (day, letter, channel_shortcut) coming from a single source row per day in web_demographics, so joining on day alone will expand by letters/channels only if the date_dim is one row per day. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to small 1:1 dimension tables keyed by letter or channel_shortcut (e.g., demographic_letter.dim_key = web_demographics_unpivot.letter or channel.dim_key = web_demographics_unpivot.channel_shortcut) — safe because those dimensions are expected to be one row per key and will not duplicate measures. | do NOT join directly to any one-to-many fact/detail table (for example, orders_with_lines_and_customers or purchases_enriched) on day without first aggregating that other table to the same grain (day, letter, channel_shortcut) — such joins would multiply this view's cnt/qty because orders/purchases are typically many per day and would duplicate the web_demographics_unpivot rows' measures. | do NOT join to sibling aggregate views that are at a coarser or many-per-day grain (e.g., product_monthly_sales) without aligning grain first; instead either (a) aggregate web_demographics_unpivot up to the sibling's grain, or (b) aggregate the other view to (day, letter, channel_shortcut) before joining. Failing to align grain will produce duplicated or incorrect sums. | safe composition pattern: to combine with web_daily_device_totals (NORM) or other day-level normalized views, join on (day) and ensure the other side is one row per day (or pre-aggregated to day). If the other view has multiple rows per day (e.g., by device), aggregate it to day before joining to avoid multiplication. | safe composition pattern: to compute combined metrics (e.g., total qty by day), aggregate web_demographics_unpivot with GROUP BY day (and optionally letter/channel_shortcut) and then join aggregated results to other tables at the same grain — this preserves correct sums without duplication.

views.description: Unpivots the pre-aggregated web_demographics row into rows per day x gender x channel with counts and qty. One row per day+gender+channel exposing cnt and qty, enabling segmentation queries across genders and channels. | Use for: compare counts/qty across channels and genders; join with gender_dim or channels_dim by letter or shortcut; compute share of channel by gender and vice versa

views.name: latest_ticker_per_symbol
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  symbol,
  day,
  price,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY symbol ORDER BY day DESC) AS rn
FROM
  ticker

params.description: Provides, for each symbol and day from ticker, the price and a rank (rn) ordering rows per symbol by day descending so the most recent day has rn = 1.
params.when_to_use: Find the latest (most recent) price per symbol by selecting rows where rn = 1. | Compose time-aware metrics per symbol by filtering to the top-N most recent days per symbol (e.g., rn <= N). | Join latest-price-per-symbol into downstream dimension or reporting queries to annotate symbols with their most recent price. | Build comparison queries that need the previous price(s) per symbol by selecting rn = 1 and rn = 2 and joining on symbol.
params.output_schema: symbol: the ticker symbol (derived from ticker.symbol) | day: the date/time of the price observation (derived from ticker.day) | price: the observed price at that day (derived from ticker.price) | rn: integer rank within each symbol partition ordered by day descending; 1 = most recent (derived from RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY symbol ORDER BY day DESC))
params.metric: rn = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY ticker.symbol ORDER BY ticker.day DESC) | price = ticker.price (atomic base column, not an aggregate) | note: there are no aggregate metrics (SUM/AVG/COUNT) in this view; rn is a window function producing an ordinal per partition.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a symbol-level dimension (e.g., a products or symbols dimension that has one row per symbol) on latest_ticker_per_symbol.symbol = dim.symbol using a filter latest_ticker_per_symbol.rn = 1 — safe because after filtering to rn = 1 the view is one-row-per-symbol so measures (price) will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: when joining to other one-row-per-symbol views/tables (e.g., a normalized symbol master table) join on symbol after filtering to rn = 1 — safe for the same reason. | do NOT directly join this view (without filtering) to a one-to-many child table (e.g., orders, trades, web events) on symbol expecting measures to remain unduplicated because multiple rows per symbol (different rn values, different days) will multiply rows and duplicate price values. Either filter to rn = 1 first or aggregate/limit appropriately before joining. | do NOT join to another time-series table on (symbol, day) unless you ensure the join keys are unique on both sides. If you need to join to a many-days-per-symbol table, first reduce this view (or the other table) to the same time grain (e.g., rn = 1 for latest day) or aggregate after the join to avoid inflating counts or sums. | composition pattern for comparing ranks: to get latest and previous price per symbol, self-join this view filtered to rn IN (1,2) and pivot by rn; that pattern is safe because you control the rn filter and deduplicate by symbol as needed. | planner hint: treat rn as an ordinal selector, not a scalar aggregate. Any composition that requires aggregated measures (SUM/AVG) over the latest prices should perform the aggregation after filtering to rn = 1 to maintain correct cardinality.

views.description: Latest ticker price per stock symbol using a window rank by day. One row per symbol+day with rank, enabling downstream filtering for the most recent price per symbol (WHERE rn = 1). | Use for: get latest price per stock symbol; time series of ticker with ability to pick top N recent days; merge latest price to stock master
